primitives.name: Ingestion Health State
primitives.verbatim_quote: # Data Reliability Automation Implemented stale-data and ingestion-health tasking under `apps/web/lib/data-reliability`.
primitives.assumptions: Ingestion health is deterministic and binary; state transitions occur only upon explicit failure detection.
primitives.breakdown_regime: H_{ingest} = 0 when ingestion state is UNKNOWN or stale beyond tolerance.

layer2.mapping: GSI Bayesian freshness model maps H_{ingest} to posterior probability of data validity; GSE state machine transitions on H_{ingest} value.
layer2.telemetry: Ingestion status flag and time since last successful update.

primitives.name: Stale Data Alert Trigger
primitives.verbatim_quote: warning. - Stale data creates a TAL task. - Critical stale data escalates risk to critical.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'T_{stale}': 'time interval in seconds since last data update', 'T_{threshold}': 'fixed threshold in seconds for stale alert', 'A_{stale}': 'binary alert signal {0, 1}'}
primitives.assumptions: Alerts are triggered deterministically when T_{stale} > T_{threshold}; criticality depends on data type and tolerance.
primitives.breakdown_regime: A_{stale} = 1 when T_{stale} > T_{threshold}, A_{stale} = 0 otherwise.

layer2.mapping: GSI probabilistic freshness model computes P(T_{stale} > T_{threshold}) as risk score; GSE uses A_{stale} to initiate TAL task.
layer2.telemetry: Time since last update and alert flag.

primitives.name: Critical Stale Risk Escalation
primitives.verbatim_quote: warning. - Stale data creates a TAL task. - Critical stale data escalates risk to critical.
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'R_{risk}': 'risk level {low, medium, high, critical}', 'T_{critical}': 'threshold time in seconds for criticality'}
primitives.assumptions: Risk escalates based on data importance and staleness duration; criticality is a monotonic function of T_{stale}.
primitives.breakdown_regime: R_{risk} = critical when T_{stale} > T_{critical}, else R_{risk} = low.

layer2.mapping: GSI risk scoring model assigns R_{risk} = critical if T_{stale} exceeds T_{critical}; GSE transitions to critical state handling.
layer2.telemetry: Risk level flag and time since last update.

The core operator 'ingestion_health_state' defines a binary condition H_{ingest} ∈ {0, 1} where 1 indicates healthy ingestion and 0 indicates unhealthy. This is mapped to a Bayesian model in GSI that estimates the probability of data validity over time. When data becomes stale, defined by T_{stale} > T_{threshold}, the 'stale_data_alert' primitive triggers an alert (A_{stale} = 1), which is a derived kernel from the base ingestion state. If T_{stale} exceeds a critical threshold T_{critical}, the system escalates risk to 'critical', modeled as a deterministic function of time. These primitives form a layered logic where GSE transitions between states based on these alerts, while GSI performs probabilistic inference on data freshness. The failure mode occurs when ingestion state remains UNKNOWN, which is treated as unhealthy regardless of freshness, indicating a systemic issue in data pipeline integrity.
